chunks: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said:
"When the time enters, purification and the prayer become obligatory, and there is no prayer except with purification."

key_terms.الطَّهُورُ: ritual purification required for worship, such as wudu (ablution)
key_terms.بِطَهُورٍ: with purification; in a state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: When does purification become obligatory for prayer in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that once the time of salat (prayer) begins, taharah in the form of purification becomes obligatory along with the prayer itself. It emphasizes that salat is not valid without the required purification.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.67 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"When the time for prayer enters, purification (ablution) and the prayer become obligatory, and there is no prayer without purification."
